obtained.how: the Virginia Herpetological Society's own web pages (green frog page via getsrc; bullfrog page via curl with getsrc's user agent, saved as VHS_nd.bullfrog.html and its text VHS_nd.bullfrog.txt)

bibliography.note: Pages titled 'North American Green Frog (Lithobates clamitans)' and 'North American Bullfrog (Lithobates catesbeianus)', Virginia Herpetological Society, no date or author shown; both URLs in the entry work. Their life-history sections compile the literature (each value carries its original citation), so 'X, via VHS n.d.' is the right form.

claims.claim: Green frogs rarely go more than 1 m from water except on rainy nights (Minton 1972, via VHS n.d.)
claims.quote: adults rarely go more than 1 m from water except on rainy nights

claims.claim: Their tadpoles overwinter once; overwinters once (Martof 1952)
claims.quote: will typically, but not always, overwinter for 1 yr prior to metamorphosing
claims.conditions: cited to Martof 1952, Richmond 1964 and Vogt 1981 (range-wide); for Maine the page adds that tadpoles stay under silt and dead vegetation in winter (Hunter et al. 1999)
claims.note: In §3.8.6 the tadpole statement sits under '(Hunter et al. 1999, via VHS n.d.)', but the overwinter-once fact is Martof's (as Table 3.8-3 says); 'typically' is worth keeping.

claims.claim: Maine adults hibernate from October to March (Hunter et al. 1999, via VHS n.d.)
claims.quote: hibernate either underwater or underground from October–March (Hunter et al., 1999)

claims.claim: radio-tagged Nova Scotia bullfrogs tolerated pond oxygen partial pressures below 20 Torr for more than 8 weeks (Friet & Pinder 1990, via VHS n.d.)
claims.quote: tolerated prolonged hypoxia (sustained PO2 below 20 Torr for > 8 wk
claims.conditions: radio-tagged bullfrogs hibernating in a pond in Nova Scotia (Friet & Pinder 1990)

claims.claim: bullfrogs are not freeze-tolerant (via VHS n.d.)
Their tadpoles are relatively unpalatable to fish (Werner & McPeek 1994, via VHS n.d.)
claims.quote: relatively immune to fish predation because of unpalatability
claims.conditions: VHS cites Walters 1975, Kruse & Francis 1977, Nelson 1980, Kats et al. 1988 and Werner & McPeek 1994 together
claims.note: Werner & McPeek 1994 is one of five sources cited for it.

claims.quote: May–August in Kentucky (Barbour, 1971), Maine (Hunter et al., 1992

claims.conditions: range-wide compilation, clutch size rising with female size; second clutches near Ithaca 1,000-1,500

claims.location: web page (green frog), Features of metamorphosis
claims.quote: Tadpoles are 60–80 mm TL at metamorphosis
claims.conditions: total length; Minton 1972, Johnson 1977, Dundee & Rossman 1989, Rogers 1999 (Indiana to Louisiana and West Virginia, not Maine)

claims.claim: maturity ~1 yr after metamorphosis (Hunter et al. 1999)
claims.location: web page (green frog), Age/Size at Reproductive Maturity
claims.quote: become sexually mature about 1 yr after metamorphosis
claims.conditions: Minton 1972 and Hunter et al. 1999; in Maine females mature at 65-75 mm and males at 60-65 mm

claims.claim: males 1.0-1.5 m apart in dense vegetation, 4-6 m on open shore (Wells 1977)
claims.quote: In dense vegetation, males may be only 1.0 to 1.5 m apart.

claims.claim: up to ~20,000, in films of 0.5-1 m²
claims.location: web page (bullfrog), Egg deposition sites and Clutch size
claims.quote: Eggs are laid in thin sheets on the water surface, covering 0.5–1 m2
claims.conditions: 'up to 20,000 eggs/clutch' (Schwalbe & Rosen 1999); films from Bury & Whelan 1984

claims.claim: up to 3 yr in Michigan and Nova Scotia
claims.location: web page (bullfrog), Length of larval stage
claims.quote: from a few months in the south to 3 yr in Michigan and Nova Scotia

claims.location: web page (bullfrog), Age/Size at Reproductive Maturity
claims.quote: usually occurs in 1–2 yr in males, and 2–3 yr in females
claims.conditions: Howard 1981; Harding 1997 gives 2-4 yr to breeding size

claims.claim: territories 2-5 m across (Harding 1997); 8.8-45.8 per ha in an Illinois lake
claims.location: web page (bullfrog), Territories and density paragraph
claims.quote: 8.8–45.8 frogs/ha in a 7 ha Illinois lake
claims.conditions: males defend roughly circular territories 2-5 m in diameter (Harding 1997); density from Durham & Bennett 1963, a 7-ha Illinois lake

notes: Table 3.8-3's adult sizes are not VHS's: VHS gives green frog adults 54-90 mm (2-3.5 in) and bullfrog average 9-15.2 cm with a record 20.3 cm (8 in); the table's Maine sizes (5-10 cm; to ~20 cm) and the bullfrog's Maine breeding (air > 20 °C, mid-June-July) and 2-yr larval period come from the MDIFW pages, per the research note. Other VHS values: green frog home range ~20-200 m² (Martof 1953); bullfrog density 0.9-1.3/m² in an Ontario pond; bullfrog larval survival 11.8-17.6 % in Kentucky.
